bet.text: The team tries to build the simplest robot that meets the objectives needed to be competitive, and calls simplicity the standout feature.

demand.text: Fuel throughput: the team credits hopper capacity of almost 70 (mostly 50 to 60 in play) and moving fuel in and out quickly for its most successful season.
At the state championship it climbed only when the climb ranking point was within reach, to avoid the risk otherwise.

cycle.text: A rack intake slides out with the hopper and pulls fuel in; belts push fuel to the injector; compliant wheels feed an S-shaped path to flywheels under a hood that pops up. Limelight pose aims the shot.
Jostling the intake in and out helped keep fuel from jamming in the hopper.

endgame.text: A side "harpoon" climb with auto climb, helped by a second Limelight when the front one cannot see tags. At the state championship it was off the robot because the net could stretch over and catch on it, and no climb ranking point was in reach.

fallback.text: Under defense it shoots from the trench: the raised hood reacts against the trench, so the robot is not pushed underneath.
A poster says a drum only two fuel wide (the team says 2.75) was harder for defenders to exploit than very wide ones.
Another says its hood and the trench wall made it nearly unmovable.

gave_up.text: A front "flippy hook" climb, which got in the way of the shooter rollers.
A video ranking says the 2.75-ball-wide shooter had slightly lower throughput than full-width ones on Einstein, though still a very high rate.
The team calls shearing teeth on the polycarbonate intake racks probably its biggest pain point, never fully fixed.
It never had shoot on the move.

changed.text: Two separate shooters jammed, so the middle came out to make one full shooter.
After a partial rebuild, powered top and bottom indexing rollers jammed the chamber until the lower ones were locked.
A lower current limit once deployed reduced rack breakage for worlds.
Contact in Einstein match 13 left a shooter motor with a chipped case and disconnected CAN wire.
A partner blames another robot's intake inside its frame.

outcome.text: 70-5-0 in official play; won the Galileo division; captain of the Galileo alliance on Einstein; ranked 5 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 333.84, Galileo).

solves.text: Get balls inside the robot as fast as possible

facts.text: A 1/2 in hex shaft across the robot ties the two sides together
4 in polycarbonate tube wrapped in cat tongue, on two Kraken X60s
A 98A TPU printed idler tensions the chain and keeps the two sides in sync; the chain never skipped, and ran two events without the idler with no issues
For the world championship the deploy current limit drops from 45 A while deploying to 5 A once deployed, to make the intake more collapsible on hits
An arm swap took about
Mostly run without lubricant: printed PETG blocks on the sides and bearings above and below hold the polycarbonate; graphite was tried once
In a redesign the team would use two 1/4 in plates with teeth on both, supported underneath by the gear; a team member had earlier suggested decoupling the two sides

cost.text: Rack teeth, trouble free at two events, sheared every two to three matches at the state championship, on unused spare arms too; about 16 spares were made for the world championship, where they still sheared but less often

solves.text: Hold a lot of fuel as simply as possible

facts.text: Connected to the rack intake; about 65 to 70 fuel per hopper
Mostly 50 to 60 fuel in play
A net on top expands storage

solves.text: Funnel balls into the shooter and keep maintenance easy

facts.text: Belts on one Kraken X60 push fuel into the injector
It flips up for access to the electronics
Uses ordinary 105T x 15 mm timing belts

functions.name: Injector

solves.text: Powering top and bottom rollers pushed fuel into the chamber too fast, and friction between balls jammed it

functions.type: compliant-wheel feed with static lower surface

facts.text: Eight compliant wheels on one Kraken funnel balls to the shooter
The top rollers are powered and the lower surface is static
The print-in-place PETG vectored wheels lasted the whole season inside the robot; the team doubts they would on an intake
The wheels adapt a 2910 design: roller clearance was adjusted, because most rollers of the original fused when printed, and a 1/8 in boss lets wheels stack without spacers

functions.name: Shooter

solves.text: A static hood surface needs no external belt that a push into the trench would likely damage

functions.type: 2.75-wide flywheel shooter with pop-up static hood

facts.text: Evolved from a two-chamber shooter to a single one 2.75 wide
Two Krakens on each side power the flywheels
4 in stealth wheels run much faster than the wheels that feed them, so fuel did not jam once it reached them
A second Limelight, used only for the climb by the state championship, helps auto climb when the front one cannot see tags
A later post describes a telescoping climber with a detachable hook; the hook was off for every world championship match, as the climb ranking point was never in reach

cost.text: The net can stretch over and get caught on it, so it was off at the state championship
A net snagged on the hook could block the shooter completely, which happened in a state championship qualification match

facts.text: At the first event the Limelight went out almost every match and threw off the aim; the team found physical problems in it

cost.text: A second Limelight fought the first for position, so by the state championship it served only the climb

decisions.because: the team looked for the fastest way to get balls inside and developed both ideas
it needs no external belt, which a push into the trench would likely damage

decisions.choice: Lower indexing rollers fixed in place
decisions.because: two powered sides pushed fuel into the chamber too fast

decisions.choice: Ordinary timing belts on the floor
decisions.because: coated belts were not sold in the 105T length and recutting the side plates was not worth it

decisions.choice: Second Limelight for the climb only
decisions.because: two Limelights fought for position and spoiled the pose

decisions.choice: Climb only for the ranking point
decisions.because: without a chance at it, the team would rather not take the risk
